title: A transverse codimension-two witness for an immersive system on a finite cover
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $X$ a smooth connected affine finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension $d\ge2$, and $\pi:T\to X$ a finite etale map with T connected. Let S be any finite set of closed points, $U_0=X\setminus S$, L an invertible module, V a finite-dimensional k-vector space with finite basis b, and $\psi:V\to\Gamma(X,L)$ a k-linear map. Suppose its basis sections generate on U0 and their associated projective morphism is an immersion. Then there exist $v_1,v_2,v_3\in V$ and an irreducible closed subset W of T, maximal among those contained in $|Z(\pi^*\psi(v_2))|\cap|Z(\pi^*\psi(v_3))|$, such that W is not contained in $|Z(\pi^*\psi(v_1))|$ and has codimension exactly two. This is only condition (3) in Tag 0G4F, with no assertion about any general divisor. Scheme and morphism notions are [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], invertibility and generation are [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], the associated morphism is [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], tensor pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback], zero schemes are [def-pc-zero-scheme], connectedness is [def-weil-connected-scheme], and pure dimension is [def-weil-pure-dimension]. No vanishing on S is assumed.

proof.text: Finite etale T over affine finite-type X is affine finite type and smooth over k. Smoothness gives regular local rings; connected regular X and T are integral.

Every closed point of either finite-type $k$-scheme has residue field finite over $k$ by [lem-kun-closed-point-field], hence equal to $k$. A $k$-rational point maps to a $k$-rational, therefore closed, point under $\pi$. Since $X$ is integral of pure dimension $d$, $\dim A=d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring]. For every closed $x\in X$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring-localization] gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=d$. For every closed $t\in T$, with $x=\pi(t)$, the affine etale ring map $A\to B$ gives $\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=d$ by [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension]. Finally [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] identifies these dimensions with $\operatorname{codim}(\{x\},X)$ and $\operatorname{codim}(\{t\},T)$.

The inverse image of S is a finite set of closed points. Finiteness of pi gives finite fibres. Etaleness gives local quasi-finiteness, hence discrete fibres; the fibre over a closed point of S is closed in T, so each of its points is closed in T. A finite union of these fibres is the required finite closed set. This does not use vanishing of any section on S.

The open $T\setminus\pi^{-1}S$ is nonempty. Otherwise the underlying space of the nonempty scheme $T$ would be a finite set of closed points, with no strict generalizations; [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] would give dimension zero for all its local rings, contrary to dimension $d\ge2$ at closed points. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], closed points are dense in $T$, so choose a closed $t$ in this open and set $x=\pi(t)$. Both are $k$-rational and $x\notin S$.

Choose $v_1\in V$ with $s_1=\psi(v_1)$ nonzero at $x$, using [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre], and extend $v_1$ to a basis $v_1,e_2,\ldots,e_r$ of $V$. Near $x$, use $s_1$ as frame and put $a_i=\psi(e_i)/s_1$. By [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], these are the pullbacks of the polynomial coordinates $T_i/T_1$ on the corresponding affine chart. The assumed immersion gives a surjection from the local ring of projective space at the image of $x$ onto $\mathcal O_{X,x}$: factor it as an open immersion after a closed immersion and use [def-weil-closed-immersion]. It therefore gives a surjection on maximal ideals modulo their squares. The maximal ideal of the chart at this $k$-point is generated by $T_i/T_1-a_i(x)$ (subtracting a polynomial's value expresses it in these generators). Consequently the classes of $a_i-a_i(x)$ span $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$. They are the local coefficients of $\psi(w_i)$, where $w_i=e_i-a_i(x)v_1$ vanishes at $x$.

proof.text: For each of the two regular local rings $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal and put $e=\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Regularity and $\dim R=d$ imply $e\le d$ by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Lift a basis of this cotangent space to $e$ elements of $\mathfrak m$; they generate $\mathfrak m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], since $\mathfrak m$ is finite over the Noetherian ring $R$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $J=\mathfrak P=\mathfrak m$ gives $d\le e$, since $R/\mathfrak m=k$ has height zero. Hence $e=d$ for both local rings.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK); regular local ring definition and the Noetherian height bound

proof.text: Because $\pi$ is etale it is unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. At the rational points $t,x$, [lem-sc-rational-unramified-cotangent-criterion] gives a surjection $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2\to\mathfrak m_t/\mathfrak m_t^2$. Thus the pulled-back classes of $a_i-a_i(x)$ span the latter space, of dimension $d\ge2$. Choose two $k$-linear combinations of the $w_i$, denoted $v_2,v_3$, whose pulled-back coefficients have independent cotangent classes at $t$. Their coefficients at $x$ are also independent, since any relation at $x$ would pull back to a relation at $t$. The sections $\psi(v_2),\psi(v_3)$ vanish at $x$, their pullbacks vanish at $t$, and $\psi(v_1)$ and its pullback are nonzero at these points.

In each local ring $R$ of step 8, let $f,g$ be the coefficients of these two sections in the frame $\psi(v_1)$ or its pullback. Their independent classes extend to a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$; lifting the rest and applying [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] extends $f,g$ to a minimal set of $d$ generators of $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $R/(f)$ and $R/(f,g)$ are regular local rings of dimensions $d-1,d-2$. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], they and $R$ are domains. Thus $(0)\subsetneq(f)\subsetneq\mathfrak p=(f,g)$ is a strict chain of prime ideals: $f\ne0$ and $g\notin(f)$ follow from their independent cotangent classes. The height of $\mathfrak p$ is at least two. It is at most two by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $J=\mathfrak P=\mathfrak p$ and two generators, because $\mathfrak P/J=0$ has height zero in the domain $R/\mathfrak p$. Hence $\operatorname{ht}_R(\mathfrak p)=2$.

source.place: Tags 00DV (lemma-NAK), 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), 00NP (lemma-regular-domain) and the Noetherian height bound

proof.text: For each pair $(Y,y)=(X,x),(T,t)$ choose an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ on which the chosen frame is invertible; write the section coefficients as $f,g\in C$ and $R=C_{\mathfrak m_y}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], the prime $(f,g)R$ contracts to a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m_y$ of $C$. It is minimal over $(f,g)C$: a smaller prime containing this ideal would extend to a smaller prime containing the prime ideal $(f,g)R$, which is impossible. The same inclusion-preserving prime correspondence identifies all chains below $\mathfrak q$ with chains below $(f,g)R$, so $\operatorname{ht}_C\mathfrak q=2$. By [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], $V(\mathfrak q)$ is an irreducible component of the intersection of the two zero schemes inside $W$.

source.place: Tags 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization) and 00ES (lemma-irreducible, minimal-prime components), applied to the quotient C/(f,g)

proof.text: Take the closure in T of the affine minimal-prime component through t. The open-subspace order correspondence shows it is maximal in the global two-section intersection. Its generic point has coheight two. Since the first section is nonzero at t, this component is not contained in its zero locus.

theorem bertini_finiteCover_transverse_component
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsAffine X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [Smooth (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hdim : X.IsPureDimension d)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace T] (π : T ⟶ X) [IsFinite π] [Etale π]
    (S : Finset X) (hclosed : ∀ x ∈ S, IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (U₀ : X.Opens) (hU₀ : (U₀ : Set X) = (S : Set X)ᶜ)
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    (r : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) k V) (ψ : V →+ Γ(L, ⊤))
    (hlinear : ∀ (c : k) (v : V),
      ψ (c • v) = (X ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv c) • ψ v)
    (hgen : Epi (((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback U₀.ι).obj L).freeHomEquiv.symm
      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _
        (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection _
          (Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionsUnit U₀.ι L (ψ (b i.down)))))))
    [IsImmersion (@ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections
      (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) inferInstance U₀.toScheme (Spec (.of k))
      (U₀.ι ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k))) ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback U₀.ι).obj L)
      (Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible.of_iso
        (((Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction U₀.ι)).leftAdjointUniq
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction U₀.ι)).app L).symm)
      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _
        (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection _
          (Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionsUnit U₀.ι L (ψ (b i.down))))) hgen)] :
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback π).obj L).IsInvertible :=
      Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible.of_iso
        (((Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction π)).leftAdjointUniq
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction π)).app L).symm
    ∃ (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (W : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds T),
      Maximal (fun Z : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds T ↦
        (Z : Set T) ⊆
          (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback π).obj L)
            (Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionsUnit π L (ψ v₂))).zeroLocus.support ∩
          (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback π).obj L)
            (Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionsUnit π L (ψ v₃))).zeroLocus.support) W ∧
      ¬ (W : Set T) ⊆
        (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback π).obj L)
          (Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionsUnit π L (ψ v₁))).zeroLocus.support ∧
      Order.coheight W = 2
